subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should configured model-ref validation be advisory, strict fail-closed, or limited to known-retired/suppressed catalog entries?
rationale: Provider routing, config validation, and fallback behavior are compatibility-sensitive, and source inspection cannot safely choose how authoritative the catalog should be for custom or future model refs.

options.title: Advisory trusted-catalog validation
options.body: Warn in `config validate` and doctor when a configured ref is absent from trusted runtime/catalog evidence, while allowing custom and future refs with clear wording.

options.title: Strict fail-closed validation
options.body: Reject configured refs not present in the trusted catalog, reducing runtime surprises but risking breakage for custom providers and newly released models.

options.title: Keep suppression-only validation
options.body: Continue only blocking known-retired or explicitly suppressed refs, preserving maximum compatibility but leaving the reported class mostly unresolved.

recommendation.title: Advisory trusted-catalog validation
recommendation.body: Warn in `config validate` and doctor when a configured ref is absent from trusted runtime/catalog evidence, while allowing custom and future refs with clear wording.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to recent config validation and model-routing helper history.
